rv.q: But for a glorious slice of camp escapism, executed at the highest possible standard, this show is hard to beat.
No room to interrogate his status as an abusive incel here, just a good yarn.
Lent a hand by Lloyd Webber’s sumptuous tunes, so too does this Phantom.
Claire Allfree hails his “masterful miniature portrait of hapless humanity”.
This musical has an unmistakably elegant froideur about it, making it easier to admire than love.
For Dave Fargnoli , it is a "sweet-natured comedy" that "gently probes tensions between social classes".

Lost since the days of Michael Crawford and Sarah Brightman is a measure of acting ability, but if Rauch and Escobar are rather stiff (her in particular) then they do enough to successfully ride the wave of this still awesome spectacle.
Fein’s production looks and sounds sumptuous, yet it’s a little like an expensive chocolate box, with nothing within that offers any fresh or surprising flavour.
The cast were all wonderful with Killian Donnelly showing his diverse acting and singing talent
